examples.en: I sent a postcard to my family from my trip.

examples.ko: 박물관 기념품 가게에서 그림엽서를 몇 장 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a few postcards at the museum gift shop.
The postcard my friend sent arrived today.

examples.ko: 이 그림엽서는 제주도 풍경이 아주 예뻐요.
examples.en: The Jeju Island scenery on this postcard is very pretty.
I wrote a short greeting on the back of the postcard.

examples.ko: 책상 앞 벽에 그림엽서 두 장을 붙여 놓았어요.
examples.en: I stuck two postcards on the wall in front of my desk.

explain: 그냥 '엽서'라고 해도 돼요. '그림엽서'는 한쪽에 그림이나 사진이 있는 엽서를 말해요. 보통 '그림엽서를 쓰다, 보내다, 부치다'처럼 말하고, 세는 단위는 '장'이에요.

phrases.en: I wrote a postcard to my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그림이나 사진이 없는 엽서까지 포함하는 더 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word that includes postcards without pictures or photos.

phrases.en: I mailed a picture postcard at the post office.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels more like putting it in the mail than 'send'.

phrases.en: I bought one picture postcard as a souvenir.

explain_en: You can simply say '엽서' too; '그림엽서' is one with a picture or photo on one side. It is usually '그림엽서를 쓰다, 보내다, 부치다', and the counter is '장'.

examples.en: I watched this cartoon with Korean dubbing.
The dubbing felt awkward, so I watched it again with subtitles.
A famous voice actor took on the dubbing of the main character.
Children like dubbed movies.
Is there an English dubbed version, too?
I played a movie dubbing game with my friend.

explain: 더빙은 목소리를 다른 말로 바꿔 넣는 것이고, 자막은 글자로 보여 주는 거예요. 그래서 '더빙으로 보다', '자막으로 보다'처럼 나눠서 말해요. 더빙을 하는 사람은 '성우'라고 불러요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 목소리를 바꾼 버전으로 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for watching the version with replaced voices.

phrases.en: This movie has a Korean dub.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the version voiced in Korean.

phrases.en: A voice actor dubs the movie into Korean.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-하다'를 붙이면 목소리를 바꿔 넣는 동작이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-하다' makes it the action of dubbing.

explain_en: Dubbing replaces the voices, while subtitles show the words as text. So people say '더빙으로 보다' or '자막으로 보다'. People who do the voices are called '성우' (voice actors).

en: to be turned inside out; to be turned upside down

examples.en: The wind was strong, so my umbrella turned inside out.
My sock is inside out, so it's uncomfortable to wear.
The clothes came out of the washing machine inside out.
The drawer flipped over, so everything spilled out.
The flipped-over turtle is struggling.

examples.ko: 프라이팬 위의 전이 잘 뒤집어지면 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: I feel good when the Korean pancake (jeon) in the pan flips over well.

explain: '뒤집다'는 사람이 하는 일이고, '뒤집어지다'는 힘을 받아서 저절로 뒤집히는 일이에요. 비슷한 '뒤집히다'가 더 자주 쓰여서 우산이나 결과가 바뀔 때는 '뒤집혔어요'가 더 흔해요. 소리는 [뒤지버지다]로 이어서 읽어요.

phrases.example: 그 영상이 너무 웃겨서 다 같이 뒤집어졌어요.
phrases.en: to crack up; to roll with laughter
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 웃겨서 정신을 못 차릴 정도일 때 입말에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Casual speech for laughing so hard you cannot control yourself.

explain_en: '뒤집다' is something a person does; '뒤집어지다' is something that flips by itself under force. The similar '뒤집히다' is more common, so for umbrellas or results changing, '뒤집혔어요' is the usual choice. The sound links, so it is read as [뒤지버지다].

en: to be fruitful; to be effective; to be paying

examples.en: Teaching children is rewarding.
The volunteer work was a truly rewarding time.
I want to spend my day in a worthwhile way.
It was hard, but it was rewarding.
I found a rewarding and fun job.
If it is worthwhile work, I will see it through.

explain: '보람 있다'와 거의 같게 써요. '보람이 있어요', '보람을 느껴요'처럼 명사 '보람'으로도 많이 말해요. 자기 노력에 대한 만족을 말할 때 어울려요.

phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as 보람되다.

phrases.en: I feel fulfilled when I help students.
phrases.nuance_en: A common expression that uses the noun 보람.

phrases.en: Today was a really rewarding day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 쓰는 활용형으로 하루나 시간을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form placed before a noun, used to describe a day or time.

explain_en: It works almost the same as 'boram itda'. People also use the noun: 'borami isseoyo' and 'borameul neukkyeoyo'. It suits satisfaction about your own effort.

examples.ko: 부산에서 온 친구가 서울말을 쓰려고 노력해요.
examples.en: My friend from Busan is trying to speak the Seoul way.

examples.ko: 서울말과 부산 사투리의 차이를 이제는 구별할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can now tell the difference between Seoul speech and the Busan dialect.
If you watch dramas, your Seoul-style speech improves naturally.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 서울말도 잘하고 사투리도 잘해요.
examples.en: That actor is good at both Seoul speech and dialects.
The Seoul accent was unfamiliar, so it was hard at first.

examples.ko: 표준어는 교양 있는 사람들이 두루 쓰는 현대 서울말로 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: The standard language is defined as the modern Seoul speech widely used by educated people.

explain: 서울 지역에서 쓰는 말이에요. 표준어는 서울말을 바탕으로 정해졌지만 둘이 똑같은 건 아니에요. 지역 말은 '사투리'나 '방언'이라고 해서, 서울말과 대비해서 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I speak in Seoul dialect when I'm on the phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 말투로 말하는지 나타낼 때 '-로'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-로' to say which way of speaking you use.

phrases.en: I learn Seoul dialect by watching dramas.
phrases.nuance_en: A pair of words Korean learners often use.

phrases.en: The Seoul dialect accent sounds soft.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말의 높낮이나 느낌을 말할 때 '억양'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '억양' to talk about the pitch or feel of speech.

explain_en: It is the speech used in the Seoul area. The standard language is based on Seoul speech, but the two are not exactly identical. Regional speech is called '사투리' or '방언', and it is often contrasted with 서울말.

examples.en: If you go to the Arctic, you can see the aurora.

examples.ko: 저는 오로라를 보러 아이슬란드에 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to go to Iceland to see the aurora.
The aurora glows green in the night sky.
I watched a video about the aurora.
The aurora also shows well only when there are no clouds.
The shape of the aurora differs every time.

explain: 한국에서는 보기 어려워서 주로 영화나 여행 이야기에서 듣게 돼요. 같은 현상을 '북극광'이라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '오로라'라고 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The northern lights shine in the night sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 현상을 부르는 다른 말이에요. 일상에서는 '오로라'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another name for the same thing; 오로라 is more common daily.

phrases.example: 겨울에 오로라를 보는 게 제 꿈이에요.
phrases.en: My dream is to see the aurora in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오로라를 직접 볼 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when seeing the aurora in person.

phrases.en: I'm planning an aurora trip with a friend.
phrases.nuance_en: A trip made to see the aurora.

explain_en: It is hard to see in Korea, so you mostly hear it in movies and travel talk. The same phenomenon is also called '북극광', but people more often say '오로라'.

en: to be in fashion; to be in

examples.ko: 요즘 학생들 사이에서 이 노래가 유행해요.
examples.en: This song is popular among students these days.
This style was really in fashion last year.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 지금 많이 유행하고 있어요.
examples.en: This outfit is very much in fashion now.
I tried a food that's trendy these days.

examples.ko: 이 춤은 곧 유행할 것 같아요.
examples.en: This dance looks like it will become popular soon.
The flu is going around, so please wear a mask.

explain: 노래, 옷, 음식뿐 아니라 독감처럼 퍼지는 병에도 '유행하다'를 써요. 하지만 가수나 배우 같은 사람에게는 쓰지 않고 '인기가 많다'라고 해요. '유행을 타다'처럼 명사 '유행'으로도 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 이 모자는 유행을 타서 내년에는 못 쓸 것 같아요.
phrases.en: to be subject to trends; to go in and out of fashion
phrases.nuance_ko: 한때 인기가 있다가 시간이 지나면 사라지는 물건이나 스타일에 써요. 오래 입을 수 있는 옷은 '유행을 안 타요'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for things or styles that are popular for a while and then fade. Clothes that last are described as '유행을 안 타요'.
phrases.en_equiv: go in and out of fashion

explain_en: '유행하다' is used for songs, clothes and food, and also for spreading illnesses like the flu. It is not used for people such as singers or actors; for them say '인기가 많다'. The noun '유행' also appears in '유행을 타다'.

dis.h: standard word for something being trendy
